source: session finding under task-061 (2026-08-11); promoted to a task by Erik via /work 2026-08-11
title: Fix [Latest Match Rate] and [Latest Coverage Rate] — both BLANK by construction
description:
Both quality measures return BLANK in every filter context. This is a computation defect, not a data gap, and it is already diagnosed with live measurements in docs/dax_measure_library.md:235 (written under task-061, 2026-08-11) — read that note first rather than re-deriving it.

Root cause: `VAR LatestRun = MAXX(gold_quality_history, gold_quality_history[refresh_timestamp])` takes the max over the WHOLE table, but two notebooks append to gold_quality_history in the same pipeline run, each stamping its own pipeline_run_ts. `silver_to_gold` writes coverage_rate / match_rate; `data_quality_checks` then writes only dq_* rows roughly ten minutes later. The later timestamp therefore always wins and never carries either metric, so the `refresh_timestamp = LatestRun` and `metric_name = "..."` filters intersect to nothing. Measured on the live model: 111 match_rate rows exist, newest at 2026-08-11T04:06:33 with value 99.42, while the table max is 2026-08-11T04:17:09 (producer data_quality_checks, all dq_*).

TWO defects, not one — a naive fix ships the second. The producers write WHOLE percentages (85 means 85%) while the measures' format string is `0.0%`, which expects a fraction. Resolving LatestRun alone would render 99.42 as 9941.8%. Fix both or neither.

Candidate approach (not prescriptive): resolve the latest run per metric via CALCULATE(MAX(refresh_timestamp), ALLEXCEPT(...), metric_name = "..."), or filter on the `producer` column so only silver_to_gold rows compete for the max. Both measures share the identical pattern and must move together — task-061 noticed only Match Rate; Coverage Rate is blank the same way.

Do not commit or push. Per the project rule, a push to main fires a real Fabric publish — the deploy and the in-report confirmation are Erik's half.
acceptanceCriteria: Both [Latest Match Rate] and [Latest Coverage Rate] return a non-blank value, verified against the live published model (offline DEFINE MEASURE evaluation is acceptable evidence for this half, as it was for task-061).

The whole-percentage vs 0.0% format-string mismatch is resolved so the rendered value reads as the true percentage (99.42% for the measured newest match_rate row, not 9941.8% and not 0.99%). State explicitly which side was changed — the measure or the format string.

The latest run is resolved per metric (or per producer) rather than by a table-wide MAX, so a later data_quality_checks append cannot re-blank either measure. Demonstrate this with a case where a dq_* row carries the table max.
Both measures are changed together and remain structurally identical to each other.
docs/dax_measure_library.md:235's 'Both currently return BLANK — known defect' note is replaced with the shipped behaviour; the diagnosis is preserved as history rather than deleted outright.
Erik's half: deploy and confirm in oem_report that both measures render a sensible percentage on a card with no slicer.
notes:

The measured evidence in docs/dax_measure_library.md:235 is the starting point — it was produced against the live model, not inferred. Re-measure before changing anything, but do not repeat the diagnosis from scratch.
